     Arsenite of Antimony. (Sb2O3) As O5 + 3 p. c.

     Prepared first by Papilland and Mousnier and introduced in the Old School practice under the name of antimonial granulations.

     Proved by Isnard and Used by Payr in emphysema.

   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Ant. ar.]
Rush of blood to head.
Pain in forehead.
Pressure in temples.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Ant. ar.]
Pain in orbits.
Inflammation of eyes.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Ant. ar.]
Œdema of face.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Ant. ar.]
Loss of appetite.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Ant. ar.]
Nausea.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Ant. ar.]
Slight diarrhœa, without pain in abdomen.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Ant. ar.]
(OBS :) Excessive dyspnœa. θ Emphysema.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Ant. ar.]
Pulse 90.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Ant. ar.]
Wandering pains along sciatic nerves.
   

NERVES. [36] [Ant. ar.]
General sick feeling.
Sense of weakness.
   

RELATIONS. [48] [Ant. ar.]
Similar to : other antimony salts ; Ammon. carb. ; Arsen. ; Aurum ; Laches. ; Merc. sulph. ; Phosphor. ; Pulsat. (ischias, wandering pains) ; Sulphur.
